definitions.explanation: The land along the edge of a lake. Refers to the shore area itself, not the water.

examples.japanese: {湖岸|こがん}を{散歩|さんぽ}した。
examples.english: I took a walk along the lakeshore.

examples.japanese: {湖岸|こがん}にホテルが{並|なら}んでいる。
{琵琶湖|びわこ}の{湖岸|こがん}は{自然|しぜん}が{豊|ゆた}かで、キャンプに{最適|さいてき}な{場所|ばしょ}だ。
examples.english: The shores of Lake Biwa are rich in nature and an ideal place for camping.

notes:
A compound of {湖|こ} (lake) and {岸|がん} (shore; bank). The {岸|がん} reading is the on'yomi form used in formal compounds.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {湖岸|こがん}を{歩|ある}く: to walk along the lakeshore
- {湖岸|こがん}{沿|ぞ}い: along the lakeshore
- {湖岸|こがん}{道路|どうろ}: lakeside road
- {湖岸|こがん}{地域|ちいき}: lakeside area

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {湖畔|こはん}: lakeside — more literary and atmospheric; often used for scenic or resort settings ({湖畔|こはん}のホテル "a lakeside hotel")
- {海岸|かいがん}: seashore; coast — the coastal equivalent, using {海|うみ} (sea) instead of {湖|こ} (lake)
- {河岸|かわぎし}/{河岸|かし}: riverbank — the river equivalent
- {岸辺|きしべ}: water's edge; shore — a more poetic, general term for any body of water
